Dalis Nilson is a master's student in data science at Boston College with a background in medicine. She is interested in measuring flourishing and distress across cultures, healthcare worker burnout and well-being, and applied machine learning for health.

As a research assistant at Harvard's Human Flourishing Program, she conducts the South Africa site analysis of the REACH Forgiveness randomized controlled trial. At Boston College, she builds Python workflows to study how children and educators around the world use ScratchJr. Before data science, she studied medicine at the University of South Florida and redesigned clinical skills curricula for hybrid and virtual instruction.

She is seeking applied data science and machine learning roles in health.

## Outside of work

I have been a hobby woodworker for years and love to spend time in my garage shop. I also paint, and one of my paintings, [*Fear*](https://hekint.org/2017/01/26/fear/), was published in the *Hektoen International Journal of Medical Humanities*. There is also a drum set in my house waiting for me to learn how to play it. I live in Austin, Texas.
